title: Field notes: sizing and cudaAlloc retry patterns under mixed KV/workspace load
content:
Summary:

These are field notes from an on-call / experiment period focused on a recurring class of OOMs we observed in mixed KV-cache + ephemeral workspace workloads. The failures manifest as: short-lived cudaMalloc retries (100–400ms stalls), intermittent allocation failures that temporarily recover after background frees, and long-tail p99 latency spikes. This doc collates traces, hypotheses, and a prioritized playbook to reduce user-visible OOMs without drastic workspace over-provisioning.

Key observations (high level):
- Two distinct allocation behaviors:
  1) small, fragmented allocations (sub-64KB) for K/V cache metadata and metadata slabs; frequent, many small frees.
  2) large, transient workspace requests (0.5–4GiB) for attention/beam inner loops; short-lived but high peak.
- cudaMallocAsync path shows fewer visible stalls for small allocations but increases tail risk under heavy concurrent streams because of deferred free timing.
- cudaMalloc (sync) sometimes triggers immediate OOM and host-side retries (we observe retry loops in runtime that back off 30–200ms). These retries correlate with increased request latencies and cascading backpressure.
- Memory pressure signals often appear in telemetry as many small free events immediately preceding a successful large allocation — implies a reactive eviction or deferred free consolidated a few hundred ms later.

Telemetry & how we looked:
- Captured per-request allocation traces with: allocator.event(logical_time, op, size, stream_id, arena_id, backtrace_id).
- Aggregated by 1s windows: count(small_allocs < 64KB), count(large_allocs > 128MB), total_reserved_bytes, resident_gpu_bytes.
- Correlated with runtime/gpu metrics: NVML reserved vs used, GPU memory utilization, CUDA stream stalls.
- Useful queries (examples for loki/temporalized view):
  - SELECT sum(small_allocs) GROUP BY window(1s), model_version
  - SELECT percentile(p99, allocator_retry_ms) GROUP BY stream
  - Filter traces where "cuda_retry_count > 0" and join with request_id to compute tail-latency impact.

Representative traces (synthesized):
- Request A (peak 3.2 GiB workspace): initial cudaMalloc failed -> runtime performed 4 host-side retries spaced 60ms -> background freeing of inactive K/V slabs observed between retry #2 and #3 -> retry #4 succeeded -> request incurred 260ms stall and succeeded.
- Request B (many small allocations): continuous small allocate/free churn during concurrent inference; fragmentation increased resident+reserved gap by ~650MB over 30s even without new large allocations.

Hypotheses:
1) Fragmentation amplification: allocator arenas per-stream/ per-device create fragmentation pockets when small allocations dominate. Over time pockets prevent a contiguous chunk large enough for the ephemeral workspace request.
2) Deferred-free timing in cudaMallocAsync keeps memory logically reserved until the CUDA stream hits a synchronization point; under high concurrency that deferral accumulates and prevents large contiguous allocations.
3) The runtime's host-side retry/backoff loop masks the underlying memory pressure instead of triggering graceful fallback, which increases p99 and hides failing requests in logs.
4) KV cache growth (eviction lag) increases reserved footprint even when resident usable contiguous memory is low; simple reserved memory metrics are insufficient for largest-contiguous-chunk prediction.

Experiments performed (and results):
- Experiment 1: Force synchronous frees (cudaDeviceSynchronize after frees) in dev builds to evaluate deferral cost. Result: reduced retry counts by ~60% for large allocations at cost of increased CPU stalls; p50 unaffected, p99 reduced but CPU utilization spiked.
- Experiment 2: Per-stream arena compaction on low-activity streams: perform one-time coalesce on allocator when fragmentation threshold exceeded. Result: recovered contiguous regions in ~40% of cases, avoided OOM in ~22% of observed incidents.
- Experiment 3: Small-allocation slab pooling (grouped 4K -> 64K): reduced small-allocation churn and gap between reserved and resident by ~350MB over 60s during high small-alloc load.
- Experiment 4: Retry policy change (aggressive early-fallback): if retry loop exceeds 3 attempts within 250ms, route request to lower-memory model variant instead of continuing to retry. Result: eliminated long-tail stalls but increased error-mode routing by ~0.8% — acceptable as temporary mitigation.

Mitigation playbook (prioritized):
1) Short-term (safe, can push to prod quickly):
   - Implement retry policy with early fallback: 3 retries max, then automatic variant fallback. Add metric and alert for fallback rate.
   - Reduce default deferred-free window for cudaMallocAsync when device free rate is low (config flag: allocator.deferred_free_ms default 200 -> 80). Toggleable per-customer.
   - Add runtime gauges: largest_contiguous_free_chunk_bytes sampled every 500ms (best-effort via allocator internal free list scan) and expose in console.
2) Medium-term (requires QA/bench):
   - Slab-pool for small allocations used by KV cache and metadata; implement size-classes to avoid small-fragment churn.
   - Arena compaction job: background incremental coalesce of adjacent free blocks with low CPU budget, enabled during low utilization windows.
3) Long-term (architectural):
   - Reservation-aware scheduler: pre-reserve workspace chunks at request admission time using predicted sequence-length distribution; if reservation fails, queue or fallback before execution to avoid mid-run OOM.
   - Hybrid allocation strategy: mix of cudaMallocAsync for small ops + a contiguous eviction-aware allocator for large workspace requests that prefers to carve from a reserved slab.

Telemetry and SLO changes recommended: 
- New SLO: 99th-mem-allocation-latency < 150ms for workspace allocations.
- New telemetry: fallback_rate_by_model, largest_contiguous_free_chunk_p50/p95, deferred_free_accumulation_ms.
- Dashboard: per-model timeline showing reserved vs resident vs largest_contiguous_free and overlay of retry events.

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Alert fires: "allocation_retry_rate>5% over 5m"
  1) Check dashboard: largest_contiguous_free_chunk and reserved-resident gap.
  2) If largest_contiguous_free_chunk < typical workspace size for that model, enable immediate mitigation: reduce per-request max_batch_size by 20% and enable fallback routing.
  3) If deferred_free_accumulation_ms > 150ms, temporarily lower allocator.deferred_free_ms and observe 5m trend.
  4) If fallback_rate skyrockets, roll back changes that increase CPU stalls (e.g., immediate synchronizations) and open incident.

Open action items / experiments to run next:
- Experiment A: Evaluate contiguous-chunk estimator based on scatter-gather free list sampling (cheap bloom-ish estimator) vs full scan; measure false positive/neg rate on production traces.
- Experiment B: Quantify cost of per-device reserved slab of 8GiB for high-tier customers: latency improvement vs cost. Add to Dedicated pricing discussion if wins are large.
- Experiment C: Run longer 24h soak with slab pooling enabled and compare fragmentation slope to baseline.
- Engineering spike: implement a debug-only allocator mode that emits a "contiguity heatmap" for ten minutes per node for deeper offline analysis.

Notes and provenance:
- Tests executed on rtx-a6000 fleet with CUDA 12.1, driver 535.XX. Runtime build: serving-runtime@commit: 1c3a9f2.
- Observed behavior changes slightly between CUDA 11.8 and 12.1 in deferred-free timing; we saw earlier release of cached blocks in 12.1 in some microbenchmarks.

Conclusions (brief):
- Primary risk driver is mismatch between many small, long-lived allocations (KV-cache/metadata) and bursty large workspace requests. Deferred-free semantics and per-stream arenas amplify fragmentation.
- Short-term mitigations (early-fallback, reduced deferred-free ms, small-slab pooling) are high ROI and low-risk and should be rolled as experiments to prod.
- Medium- and long-term efforts (compaction, reservation-aware scheduling, hybrid allocators) will reduce overall unit cost and improve reliability but require careful benchmarking.

Appendix: useful logs and grep examples:
- grep pattern for retry traces: "allocator.*cuda_retry_count>0" or "cudaMalloc returned out of memory"
- sample allocator trace format: "ts=169706... alloc_id=1234 op=malloc size=2147483648 arena=3 stream=12 retry_count=2"

Recorded by: Ravi Patel, eng-serving-runtime.
